sources.title: Library of Congress, Country Profile: Philippines, March 2006
sources.note: Direct PDF, historical background pp. 1 to 5. Used for historical relationships and chronology, not current officeholders or statistics. The map observation comes from decoded local geometry, documented in identities.json.

sources.title: Museo Amparo, Los galeones de la plata: México, corazón del comercio interoceánico, 1565 to 1815
sources.note: Direct Spanish curatorial introduction to the 1998 exhibition, especially paragraphs 1 and 3: dates, New Spain silver, Asian silk and porcelain, and trans-Pacific cultural exchange. This independent curatorial source replaces the Met essay already heavily used by an existing runtime card.

sources.title: National Museum of the Philippines, The Anchors of the Galleon San Jose, 8 November 2021
sources.note: Direct institutional article: 1694 loss, 1986 excavation and October to November 2019 expedition. The source has unrelated typographical errors in its Bronze Age sentence and cargo description; neither is used.

sources.title: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, The Philippine-American War, 1899 to 1902
sources.note: Original indexed historical essay, paragraphs on the 1898 settlement, outbreak on 4 February 1899, Aguinaldo capture, declaration of the war ending and continuing resistance. This is an archived historical account.

sources.title: National Historical Commission of the Philippines, Philippine Republican Seals in the Visayas
sources.note: Official indexed opening explicitly dates the First Republic to 23 January 1899 at Barasoain Church, Malolos. Direct page extraction timed out. Used only for this founding fact, not an uninspected original seal transcription.

sources.title: Senate of the Philippines, History of the Senate
sources.note: Full original indexed institutional history: 1916 Jones Law, reserved U.S. powers, Commonwealth inauguration on 15 November 1935, 1940 bicameral restoration, 1972 closure and post-1986 constitutional government. Direct fetch returns 403; outdated present-officeholder text is not used.

sources.title: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, Recognition and Diplomatic Relations: Philippines
sources.note: Official original indexed recognition section: U.S. recognition on 4 July 1946, proclamation and treaty renouncing claims of sovereignty. Not confused with the revolutionary declaration in 1898.

sources.title: Ricardo De Los Santos, Ghosts of Martial Law, NHCP, posted 4 September 2012
sources.note: Full official indexed article read; direct fetch returns 403. Only stable historical claims in opening and closing historical paragraph used: 1972 repression/censorship and 1986 overthrow. Contemporary political commentary, legal allegations and inferred motivations are excluded.

sources.title: Proclamation No. 2045, 17 January 1981, Philippine legal text via Lawphil
sources.note: Primary proclamation formally terminates martial law on 17 January 1981. Its celebratory statements about the regime are not adopted. Formal termination is distinguished from the continued Marcos presidency.

sources.title: Supreme Court E-Library, 1987 Constitution of the Philippines
sources.note: Full official indexed text: ratification 2 February 1987, Articles II, XIV sections 2 and 6 to 8, and Article XVIII. Legal obligations are not presented as proof of universal implementation.

sources.title: Civil Service Commission, Patalastas Bilang 04, s. 2023, 13 February 2023
sources.note: Direct original announcement, dated heading and paragraph quoting Article XIV section 6. Exact short Filipino text verified; parallel English constitutional provision supplies translation. This is a 2023 Latin-script witness quoting the 1987 constitution, not a colonial manuscript.

sources.title: Intramuros Administration, Casa Manila Museum
sources.note: Direct and full official indexed museum guide: reconstructed affluent late-colonial household, 1850s Binondo facade model; mezzanine, ventanillas, paminggalan, nievera, letrina and azotea/aljibe. It is a museum reconstruction, not a surviving universal Filipino home. The source marks a claim about the oldest objects for verification; it is omitted.

sources.title: Department of Education, Historical Perspective of the Philippine Educational System
sources.note: Full official indexed institutional history: 1863 educational decree and 1901 Act No. 74. Six hundred American teachers were authorized; the figure is not represented as the exact passenger count on one ship.

sources.title: U.S. National Park Service, Maria Ylagan Orosa
sources.note: Direct biographical essay: food preservation, 1925 Manila Carnival display, 1930s banana ketchup, palayok oven and community extension. No claim that tomatoes cannot grow in the Philippines; no unverified invention tally.

sources.title: IRRI, In Retrospect: IRRI Annual Report 1966
sources.note: Original institute publication reproducing 1966 report: IR8 trials in 1965 to 1966, short non-lodging plant form, varied growing conditions and November naming. No universal yield guarantee or unsupported invention-first claim.

sources.title: Robert F. Chandler Jr., An Adventure in Applied Science: A History of the International Rice Research Institute
sources.note: Original institute book, printed p. 112, indexed original text: farmers received two kilograms of IR8 seed on giving name/address; 2,359 farmers in the last half of 1966, arriving by bus, bicycle or on foot. Grouped conservatively with the annual-report work for budget checks.

sources.title: National Academy of Science and Technology, The First Decade, 1988: Fe del Mundo
sources.note: Original indexed academy biography, printed p. 117: pediatrics, physician/paramedical/lay-worker training and extension to rural areas. No unsupported first-woman-at-Harvard story or improvised incubator claim is included.

sources.title: WHO, UHC Act in the Philippines: a new dawn for health care, 14 March 2019
sources.note: Official original indexed article on Republic Act 11223: automatic National Health Insurance enrollment, reforms and implementation. A law and its goals, not a measurement of universally delivered services.

sources.title: Jude Ortega, Tawi-Tawi schools need better water, hygiene and sanitation facilities, UNICEF, 9 May 2024
sources.note: Full original indexed report: Pagasinan Elementary School in Bongao, Ashraf Kasawali, two handwashing pipes with ten holes each, container connection, and three toilets with one broken and one reserved for teachers. Conditions are attributed specifically to the May 2024 report.

sources.title: UNESCO, Aklan piña handloom weaving, file 01564, inscribed 2023
sources.note: Original indexed inscription description: Pinya Bisaya leaf fibers, weighing using an old coin, loom weaving, family transmission and Schools of Living Traditions. Inscription is not the invention date.

sources.title: UNESCO, The practice of making asin tibuok, Bohol Island, file 02316, inscribed 2025
sources.note: Full original indexed 2025 Urgent Safeguarding description: coconut husks soaked for months, ash/brine process, clay pots, egg-like finished salt and family transmission. No unsupported antiquity date or dinosaur-egg nickname.

sources.title: Philippine Space Agency, A decade after Diwata-1: From crisis to capability, 27 April 2026
sources.note: Direct original anniversary article: lessons from Typhoon Yolanda in 2013, engineer training in Japan, March 2016 launch and 27 April deployment from the ISS, image processing and disaster mapping. Planned future satellites are not represented as launched.

proposedOverrides.name: Philippines
proposedOverrides.summary: An archipelago across colonial and republican governments.

batchIdentityNotes.association: No alias association with philippines, the earlier 1492 to 1530 map record.
batchIdentityNotes.mapCoverage: HB from 1650, open end. Seventeen decoded features from world-1650 to world-2010, bounding box approximately 117.129 E, 5.488 N, 126.374 E, 18.553 N. Nearly unchanged archipelago outline is not evidence of uniform colonial control or maritime sovereignty.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Distinct Spanish, revolutionary, U.S. colonial, Commonwealth, occupation, independent, dictatorship and constitutional phases. The exclusive 2027 end of the last display phase is not a predicted end of the state.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: The museum is explicitly a reconstruction of an affluent household. Modern named school conditions are dated May 2024. UNESCO inscription years date documentation, not invention. Writing is a 2023 official Latin-script quotation of a 1987 provision.
